overview.text: The Texas Blind Snake is a tiny burrowing snake of the south-western United States and northern Mexico that looks like a shiny earthworm.

identification.text: Pinkish-brown and shiny, not segmented like a worm; the eyes are just two dark dots under the head scales.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: Kansas, Oklahoma, Texas and southern New Mexico, and northern Mexico.

habitat.text: Desert, grassland, shrubland, savanna and forest.

behaviour.text: Spends almost all its time in loose soil, coming up to feed or when rain floods its burrows; often seen after spring rains.

recognise.text: Looks like a shiny pinkish earthworm with scales.
